claims.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
claims.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Panthers take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings already played in Florida once this season and left with a 5-3 win on Nov 2. The Panthers (10-7-2) beat Columbus 4-1 on Tuesday, while the Red Wings are on a four-game losing streak. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Wings last (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Panthers fifth (tied for 13th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.447) says: their chances are worth about .571, and their finishing has held them back. The Panthers’ record (.579) is about what their chances are worth.
This season, the Red Wings have been outscored 57-49, but only 34-31 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 19-11.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and leave the shooting to their forwards (4th lowest), but ice the puck a lot (29th). As for the Panthers, they forecheck harder than anyone (1st) and get into a lot of chippy games (1st). The Red Wings’ power play against the Panthers’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, especially the Panthers (1st), so expect plenty of it.

Lucas Raymond (6 G / 12 A / 18 P in 19 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 19 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 23 A / 27 P in 19 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Brady Tkachuk (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 19 GP) has a team-high ten goals, with a point in five straight games against Detroit.
John Gibson (4-6-1 / .866 SV% in 12 GS) has struggled for Detroit so far, but is expected to start. Akira Schmid (5-3-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Florida.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Luostarinen, Lundell and Devine out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.
